Split the conjunction.

For the first part, use Möbius inversion in the Dirichlet-convolution algebra:
\[
\zeta * \mu=\delta_1.
\]
Transport this identity from integer-valued arithmetic functions to \(R\) through the canonical casts \(\mathbb N\to R\) and \(\mathbb Z\to R\). These casts preserve the finite divisor sums defining convolution, so the right-hand side becomes the unit arithmetic function.

For the second part, write \(\sigma=\operatorname{re}(s)>1\). The norm of the \(n\)-th L-series term is
\[
\left\|\frac{\Lambda(n)}{n^s}\right\|=\frac{\Lambda(n)}{n^\sigma},
\]
using nonnegativity of the von Mangoldt function. Apply the standard bound \(\Lambda(n)\le \log n\). Then choose \(0<\varepsilon<\sigma-1\); eventually \(\log n\le Cn^\varepsilon\), so the terms are dominated by
\[
C n^{-(\sigma-\varepsilon)},
\]
whose series converges because \(\sigma-\varepsilon>1\). A comparison argument, with finitely many initial indices handled separately, yields `LSeriesSummable`.
